scope: Split first-progress and streaming inactivity deadlines; SDK progress handling and verification-runner improvements.

diagnosis.confirmedBridgeBehavior: The prior implementation applied the 90000 ms inactivity limit before any model output. Recreating the session restarted the same potentially slow prompt instead of allowing its first progress to arrive.
diagnosis.correction: Allow a separate initial wait, then switch to the streaming inactivity limit on real progress. Observe registered root-phase private byte counts without forwarding private content. Initialization, keepalives and failure telemetry do not reset either deadline.
diagnosis.upstreamCause: The separate user-conversation error alone does not establish whether the provider was processing a long prompt, reasoning silently, or experiencing a transport/service failure. Fusion progress omission is a supported SDK path now covered, not a proven cause of that incident.

coverage.scope: src modules observed by the Node unit-test coverage runner; not unexecuted entry points, cross-process live inference or product-feature coverage.

delayedFirstProgressRegression.executionKind: actual Codex TUI with an SDK double; no live inference
delayedFirstProgressRegression.test: test/runtime/model-context.test.mjs: production watchdog tolerates first progress after 90000 ms in the actual TUI without replay
delayedFirstProgressRegression.promptSubmissionExplanation: One delayed prompt and one distinct successful follow-up; no prompt replay.
delayedFirstProgressRegression.initialMeasurementAttempt: The TUI completed successfully but a wall-clock duration assertion failed. The fixture now measures monotonic elapsed time and cannot reply before the configured delay. The unchanged >=95000 ms assertion passed on rerun.

limitations: The live matrix checks ordinary model connectivity and workflows; no real provider stall occurred in that run. Delayed-first-progress and recovery regressions are separately labelled SDK-double checks.
No guarantee of future upstream availability, maximum-window inference, multi-hour endurance, or Linux/Windows live-model behavior.
The 18-workflow suite passed offline; its separate 108-case live matrix was not executed in this change.
Optional generated titles remain unsupported. Their exact HTTP 400 rejections are counted separately and are not successful model responses.
Historical v1/v2 and stability records were not changed, regraded or combined. Raw artifacts and frozen source remain local at the report path.
